body.statement: Suppose \(0<s\le1/2\), \(t<d/2\), the Hölder balls contain the balanced two-outcome baseline in their interiors, and the fixed periodic kernel has \(a_0>0\) and ordered nonzero Fourier weights \(a_{(j)}\asymp j^{-2r}\), with the declared covariance-profile constants wide enough to contain the derived sandwich in \(\mathrm{lem{:}fuzzy\mbox{-}legality\mbox{-}affinity}\). Under uniform \(P_X\), \(\delta_n^\star\ge c n^{-2t/(2t+d)}\) for a class constant \(c>0\). At \(h=c_hn^{-2/(2t+d)}\), every \(P_\omega\) belongs to \(\mathcal M_0\), every \(Q_\omega\) belongs to \(\mathcal M_1(cn^{-2t/(2t+d)};s,R)\), the one-record mixtures coincide exactly, and the \(n\)-record mixtures have affinity bounded away from zero. Hence \(\delta_n^\star/\delta_{n,e}^\star\to\infty\).
body.justification: This is an all-tests information bound, so it survives arbitrary higher-order correction and establishes a genuine nuisance cost.
body.gap: Kennedy et al. provide a scalar CATE fuzzy bound; the exact Hilbert null, embedded signal, and covariance-source constraint are new here.
body.consumer: It tells analysts when no regularization or nuisance learner can restore oracle sensitivity in observational conditional-distribution testing.
